thread:
Priya (PM): Quick follow-up from today's all-hands 111  need a short, actionable summary on leadership priorities and what product/sales should focus on next 6 months.

Ava (CEO): Focus: make inference predictable and cost-effective for engineers. Two main tracks: 1) accelerate Hosted adoption and developer experience; 2) close Dedicated deals where predictable latency/cost and contracts matter. Private remains the compliance option. Success metric: lower cost-per-inference at our 99th-percentile latency SLO.

Omar (GTM): For mid-market, should reps pitch Hosted first or lead with Dedicated?

Ava (CEO): Start Hosted to demonstrate value quickly. Use Hosted benchmarks to justify Dedicated when customers need throughput guarantees or isolation. We'll provide a transition checklist for sales.

Liam (Head of Product): Positioning vs cloud-managed endpoints: highlight runtime-level advantages (continuous batching, KV-cache, optimizer kernels) and the unified API across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. Call out concrete cost levers (quant profiles, routing policies).

Nina (Eng Lead): Can we publish short performance snapshots per model+hardware? Sales keep asking.

Ezra (Research): We'll produce a compact matrix: model family x accelerator -> tokens/sec and p50/p95/p99 latency. Need a few representative traces.

Liam (Head of Product): Agreed. Product will own a one-pager perf matrix + migration playbook. ETA: three weeks to publish on docs.

Omar (GTM): Competitive angle: how do we talk about big cloud providers with managed endpoints?

Ava (CEO): Three pillars: operational economics (knobs that materially change cost), deployment flexibility (same API across modes), and dev ergonomics (streaming, function calls, rollout policies). Avoid head-to-head feature lists; lead with predictable latency and cost.

Priya (PM): Pricing: what mix of usage vs committed should we aim for? Any compensation changes for AEs?

Ava (CEO): Continue self-serve usage for new signups. Push committed/Dedicated for customers crossing throughput or compliance thresholds. Short term: incentivize AEs to convert high-usage accounts to committed deals. We'll track % revenue from committed vs usage.

Nina (Eng Lead): Engineering asks that unblock Dedicated sales: 1) autoscaling with latency SLOs, 2) per-tenant KV cache controls, 3) safer rollout fallbacks. Prioritize please.

Ava (CEO): Noted. Liam, Nina, and Ezra to define acceptance criteria for these three items.

Liam (Head of Product): I'll start a working group and create a tracking board within 48 hours. Please drop customer asks there.

Omar (GTM): Can we get a standard POC playbook (Hosted -> Dedicated) so AEs don't reinvent the wheel? Even a checklist + slide deck helps.

Liam (Head of Product): In scope for the working group. We'll deliver a template POC and a short deck.

Ezra (Research): One more: open-source runtimes are improving quickly. Docs should explicitly state where our kernel/optimizer differences matter (long-context, KV savings, batch efficiency).

Ava (CEO): Good call. Docs team: add a "Why Redwood" technical appendix with targeted benchmarks and edge-case notes. reminder-bot: ping docs in 24h.

reminder-bot: Reminder sent to #docs-team in 24 hours to add "Why Redwood" appendix.

Priya (PM): Summary of action items: Liam to form working group + board; Docs to publish perf matrix and technical appendix; Product to draft POC playbook; Eng to list infra unblockers and acceptance criteria. I'll capture these in the project tracker.

Ava (CEO): Thanks everyone. We'll review progress at the next all-hands. If you have deal constraints or competitor intel, DM me or add to the board.

Omar (GTM): Adding customer notes to the board now.

Nina (Eng Lead): Adding infra notes.

Liam (Head of Product): Board and epic created: https://rwd.internal/boards/INF-POC-2026 (internal link).

Priya (PM): Closing thread. Reply here or DM Liam if you want to join the working group.

Ava (CEO): :rocket:
